payload.name: Preserve existing event when adding future plan
payload.description: When constructing memories and a new message mentions a future plan or trip for a subject who already has a past event memory, apply this before updating: keep the existing event's kind, date, and content unchanged, and add the plan as a separate memory.
content: Before updating an existing event memory with new plan or future-oriented information, check whether it describes a distinct future plan rather than a correction of the past event.
If it is a distinct future plan, ADD a new memory with memory_kind 'plan' and its own world_start; do not change the existing event's memory_kind, world_start, or content.
Do not merge plan text into an event memory; preserve the event's original temporal anchor and facts so the event remains independently queryable.

solves: During construction, a later message about a future plan or trip for the same subject can cause an UPDATE that overwrites an existing past event's memory_kind, world_start, and content, losing the original event's date and facts. This rule prevents that by treating the future plan as a separate memory and preserving the existing event's temporal anchor and kind, which applies whenever new plan information arrives for a subject with a prior related event memory.
